# Competitor

`sales.obj.core.competitor` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> An alternative the buyer is weighing, including the status quo. The discriminator is the buyer's decision set, not the market: a vendor who sells to the same market but is not in this evaluation is a market peer and belongs in ICP work, while an internal build, a half-working spreadsheet, and "we will revisit in Q3" are all competitors here because each one is a live alternative to signing. The status quo is the most frequently underweighted competitor in sales and wins more deals than any named rival — it costs the buyer nothing to choose, requires no internal approval, and never sends a losing email. This object is scoped to a deal or account, not to the company we compete with globally.


Also called: `Alternative`, `Rival`, `Incumbent`, `Status Quo`

## Constraints

- **`comp.no_disparagement`** Never attack a competitor by name to the buyer. It transferscredibility to them and reliably reads as insecurity.
- **`comp.named_before_conceding`** No competitive concession without competitor_type =named_vendor and an evidenced price.
- **`comp.status_quo_cannot_be_absent`** An open deal may not record zero competitors; theminimum is a status-quo record.
- **`comp.position_is_behavioural`** competitive_position must be evidenced by buyer behaviour,never by internal product comparison. _(soft)_


## Business rules

- **`comp.status_quo_is_always_present`** Every open deal carries a status-quo competitor whether or not one has been named. A deal with no competitor record is under-assessed, not uncontested.

- **`comp.discount_requires_a_named_alternative`** A concession justified by competitive pressure requires competitor_type = named_vendor with a name and evidence of their price. Otherwise the discount is being granted to an alternative that may not exist.

- **`comp.no_commit_without_position`** A deal with an active competitor and competitive_position = unknown must not be forecast as committed.
- **`comp.incumbent_requires_a_switching_case`** Where is_incumbent is true, a switching-cost case must exist before proposal. Beating an incumbent on features while ignoring migration cost loses to inertia, not to the rival.

- **`comp.cost_of_inaction_required_for_status_quo`** Where competitor_type is status_quo or no_decision, cost_of_inaction must be quantified. A null value means the only competitor in the deal has no counter-argument prepared.

## Actions

- **Ask who else they are evaluating** (human) — Direct, cheap,and routinely avoided out of a fear of introducing the idea. The buyer already had the idea.
- **Quantify the cost of doing nothing** (human) — Theonly argument that beats a status quo. Turns an invisible competitor into a number on a page.
- **Influence the evaluation criteria** (human) — Higher yieldthan out-featuring a rival. Whoever writes the scorecard usually wins it.
- **Build the migration and switching case** (human) — Required against an incumbent. Inertia, not the rival's product, is what actually holds the account.
- **Pre-empt their landmines** (human) — Answering a planteddoubt before the buyer raises it removes it. Answering it afterwards confirms it was worth raising.
- **Refuse a concession to an unnamed alternative** (human) — Requires the buyer to name the alternative before the price moves. Frequently ends the pressure outright.


## Evidence

- **document** · 9500 bp — An RFP vendor list or scoring matrix. Names thefield explicitly and is rarely wrong.
- **meeting_transcript** · 8800 bp — The buyer using a rival's framing. Strongevidence of an active, coached evaluation.
- **email** · 8000 bp — A written mention. Reliable for presence, silenton identity.
- **crm** · 6500 bp — Rep-logged competitor field. Biased toward named vendorsand blind to the status quo.
- **derived** · 5500 bp — Silence and momentum collapse. The only sourcethat can see the status quo at all.
- **website** · 3500 bp — Public comparison pages and logos. Says who theytarget, not who is in this deal.


## Metrics

- **competitive_deal_share** (percent) — Share of open deals with an identifiedalternative. If this is under half, the object is not being used.
- **status_quo_loss_share** (percent) — Share of losses to no-decision rather thanto a rival. Usually the largest bucket and usually untracked.
- **win_rate_by_competitor** (percent) — Calibrates historical_win_rate_bp. Requirescompetitor identity, which is why it is currently uncomputable.
- **detection_lead_time** (days) — Days from deal creation to first competitordetection. Late detection correlates with losing.
- **concession_to_unnamed_share** (percent) — Discounts granted against an alternativenobody could name. Direct measure of leverage given away.


## Examples

- **Doing nothing** — competitor_type = status_quo, name null, their_price_position free,effort_to_do_nothing trivial. The most common winner and the one with no battlecard.
- **The incumbent renewing in four months** — is_incumbent true, switching_cost high. Weare not selling a product, we are selling a migration.
- **The named rival in a three-way bake-off** — The competitor sellers actually instrumentfor, and the least dangerous of the four listed here.
- **"We might just build it internally"** — competitor_type = internal_build. Free atthe point of decision, wildly expensive afterwards, and almost never costed by the buyer.
- **The rival named only next to a price** — The classic misclassification. Logged as acompetitive deal and given a discount; is_stalking_horse true, and they were never in the evaluation.

## Metadata

owner **Sales** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Six of eleven patterns are executable, resting on the competitor, discount_pressure, proposal_sent and timeline_slip observation kinds plus derived.momentum. The highest-value gap is competitor.name — Layer 2 knows a competitor was mentioned but never which one, so win rates cannot be joined, counter-positioning cannot be selected, and every competitive deal is handled generically. closed_lost_reason is second and compounds it: losses to a rival and losses to the status quo are currently the same event, which means the single most important number this object could produce cannot be produced at all.
